To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
GTPγs, a hydrolyzation-resistant G protein, increases the TTX-R current produced by Nav1.8 through a PKA pathway.

GTPγs increases Nav1. 8 current in small diameter DRG neurons through a PKA/ PKC pathway and that the addition of fluoride to pipette solution further increases current amplitude but is not a factor that confounds G protein modulation of Nav1. 7 current.

GTPγs increases Nav1. 8 current through a protein kinase pathway and that addition of sodium fluoride to the intracellular recording solution enhances the effect of G proteins independent of aluminum.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the modulation of TTX-R sodium current in small-diamter DRG neurons.
the regulation of Nav1.9 and Nav1.8 by GTPγ and G protein activation in small-diameter sensory neurons.
the modulation of Nav1.9 and Nav1.8 channels in DRG neurons by G proteins and PKA/PKC pathways.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
G proteins can modulate Nav1.8 in small-diameter neurons, but that the effects of fluoride in this study were independent of G proteins.
GTPγs increases Nav1.9 and Nav1.8 through PKA/PKC pathways.
the Nav1.9 and Nav1.8 channels are modulated by G protein pathways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
GTPγ can modulate Nav1.8 through PKA/PKC, but that fluoride can enhance Nav1.8 by a PKA/PCK independent mechanism.
the G-protein activation by GTP-γS can increase the Nav1. 8 current through a protein kinase C pathway.
the activation of G-protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs) can modulate Nav1.8 through PKA/PKC and that the activation of these GPCRs can also increase the expression of Nav1.9 in small DRG neurons.
The main takeaway from our work is that
G proteins modulate Nav1.8 channels in small-diameter sensory neurons, and that the modulation is through a PKA and PKC pathway.
GTPγ is an important modulator of TTX-R channels.
